title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics and tool message formatting for function calling
author: Ana M. Ruiz
release_notes: Enhances OpenAI-compat function/tool calling: canonicalizes tool schema -> tool_choice mapping, emits structured tool_call/tool_response events in streaming mode, and documents SDK-level accessors for tool_choice and formatted tool messages.
description: Context: Our OpenAI compatibility layer previously supported function/tool calling at a surface level, but two gaps remain: 1) ambiguous semantics between OpenAI 'tool_choice' (which represents agent/tool selection) and our internal tool invocation format, and 2) inconsistent formatting of tool invocation messages emitted via streaming (clients expect a stable, parsable event sequence). Motivation: Make the compatibility layer deterministic for downstream clients (SDKs, customers using WebSocket/Server-Sent-Events), reduce mismatch bugs in agent integrations, and provide a documented migration path for existing customers. Changes in this PR: - Add a canonical mapping module that translates OpenAI-style tool schemas (properties/required/oneOf) into a normalized internal 'tool_choice' descriptor; this preserves OpenAI names and schema while adding explicit metadata used by our runtime for validation and routing. - Update streaming emission to include explicit event types: 'tool_call' (metadata + serialized args), 'tool_response' (status + content/type), and keep 'assistant'/'user' for backward compatibility. - Ensure tool messages in non-streaming responses include a structured 'tool_call' wrapper inside the message content when model returns a tool invocation. - Expose 'tool_choice' on SDK response objects (python/typescript) and add helpers in SDKs to pretty-print tool invocation messages and to convert between schema forms. - Add integration tests around tool_choice selection heuristics and streaming ordering guarantees; add unit tests for schema mapping edge-cases (oneOf, nullable types, nested objects). - Documentation: add migration guide and examples for SDKs and curated examples showing how to reliably parse tool events from streams. Checklist: - [x] Mapping logic implemented and unit-tested - [x] Streaming event changes implemented and integration-tested - [x] SDK adapters (python + typescript) updated - [x] Docs and changelog updated - [x] E2E run against canary runtime environment passing Notes for reviewers: Pay special attention to the mapping rules in openai_compat/tool_mapping.py (comments enumerate heuristics: prefer explicit 'oneOf' discriminators, coerce nullable -> optional, flatten additionalProperties=true for dynamic args). Backwards compatibility: streaming clients that parse raw assistant messages will still see assistant->tool wrappers for a short transition period, but robust clients should switch to the explicit event types. Migration: SDKs expose a helper `response.tool_choice` and `response.pretty_print_tool_call()`; update customer integrations to consume these instead of parsing assistant messages. Impact and rollout: This change touches the streaming path and the OpenAI-compat translation layer; we gated rollout behind a config flag `openai_compat.tool_choice_v2` (default=off) for 2 weeks, then flipped during a low-traffic window after monitoring. Testing: Added unit + integration tests; ran canary for 48h in us-west and eu-west, observing no increase in error rate and a small (2-3%) reduction in mis-parsed tool invocations. Post-merge tasks: - follow-up to propagate changelog entries to the hosted API release notes - observe metrics for 7 days to ensure no client regressions
commits: feat: add canonical tool schema -> tool_choice mapper; test: add unit tests for mapping edge cases; feat: streaming: emit tool_call/tool_response events; feat(sdk): expose tool_choice + pretty_print helpers in python/ts SDKs; docs: add migration guide and examples; fix: edge-case handling for nullable array properties
